sub_agendas_items.title: Motion - Councillor C. Kelly – Development Charges - Pt Lt 4 Concession 7 Fitzroy

attachments.attachment_title: Coverpage - Motion - C Kelly – DCs - Fitzroy.pdf
Report - Motion - C Kelly - DCs - Fitzroy.pdf

motions.motion_text:
Committee Recommendation(s)
That Council approve the prepayment for Pt Lt 4 Concession 7 Fitzroy in 1990 be recognized as payment in full, exempting $41,952 of development charges in respect of one dwelling unit.

WHEREAS the Agriculture and Rural Affairs Committee approved a development charge waiver for Pt Lt 4 Concession 7 Fitzroy, which was created in 1990; and
WHEREAS lot levies, a precursor to development charges, were prepaid in full at that time amounting to $4,152; and
WHEREAS the Development Charge rate in effect for a Singles and Semi-detached Dwelling in the Rural Area (Unserviced) is $46,104;
WHEREAS the lot falls under Rural Transit Area B where a credit of $12,608 would be applied resulting in a net charge of $33,496;
WHEREAS the established City practice has been only to recognize these prepayments as a credit on a dollar-for-dollar basis toward development charges owing; and
WHEREAS applying Ottawa’s Construction Price Index to the prepaid lot levy would recognize the value paid in 1990 of $4,152 to a 2026 value of $11,770; and
WHEREAS applying a full credit results in a discretionary exemption that must be funded from the City’s Development Charge Exemption Budget.
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that the $4,152 prepayment for Pt Lt 7 Concession 4 Fitzroy made in 1990 be indexed from the date of payment to the 2026 value of $11,770, using the Construction Price Index, and that the resulting indexed amount be recognized as a credit toward the development charges owing in respect of one dwelling unit.

sub_agendas_items.title: Special Event Road Closures and Community Notification
Private Approaches and Encroachments on Whitmore Avenue, Cline Crescent and Sherman Drive in Bel Air Heights

motions.motion_text:
WHEREAS beginning in 2027/2028 the City will undertake an integrated road reconstruction project in the Bel-Air Community neighborhood of Ward 8, including the reconstruction of Whitmore Avenue, Cline Crescent and Sherman Drive; and
WHEREAS the project limits for the Whitmore Avenue, Cline Crescent and Sherman Drive Integrated Road, Sewer and Watermain project includes reinstating some private approaches and private encroachments on Whitmore Avenue (Iris Street to the north intersection with Cline Crescent), Cline Crescent (south intersection of Whitmore Avenue to Albany Drive) and Sherman Drive (Navaho Drive to Cline Crescent); and
WHEREAS some of the driveway widths/lengths within the project limits are not in full conformance with the City’s front yard parking restrictions and Private Approach By-law; and
WHEREAS, for existing properties, front yard parking restrictions and private approach by-law and private encroachments upon City Right-of-Way are normally enforced only on a complaint-driven basis; and
WHEREAS there have been no complaints with respect to non-compliant driveways (private approaches) or front-yard parking in this area; and
WHEREAS the area residents support providing relief for residents with existing driveways (private approaches) while acknowledging that any future driveways (private approaches) and front-yard parking must be in accordance with City by-laws;
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that Council approve that, in respect of the reconstruction of Whitmore Avenue, Cline Crescent and Sherman Drive, private approaches and encroachments be reinstated as they were immediately prior to the reconstruction of this street, as practicable.

sub_agendas_items.title: Demolition Control Waiver for 72, 74, and 85 Pamilla Street

motions.motion_text:
WHEREAS the City of Ottawa and the Developer (1197692 Ontario Inc.) have entered into a Memorandum of Understanding establishing the framework for a proposed land exchange whereby 72 and 74 Pamilla Street (total 750.89m²) would be conveyed to the City in exchange for 80 Norman Street (372.28 m²) allowing the City to create a larger neighbourhood park to replace the existing McCann Park; and
WHEREAS the owner of 425 Preston Street would provide 72 Pamilla Street (375.89 m²) and 74 Pamilla Street (375.00 m²) to the City and that the additional 378.61 m² land would contribute toward their parkland dedication if/when their assembled development lands are developed; and
WHEREAS the land being provided as parkland must be conveyed to the City free of all encumbrances; and
WHEREAS the demolition of existing residential use buildings at 72 and 74 Pamilla Street is required prior to transferring the properties to the City; and
WHEREAS the current state of 85 Pamilla, part of the future development site separate from the MOU, is in poor condition and not habitable; and
WHEREAS by waiving demolition control application, the City will not receive $6,200.48 (includes $1,274.64 Legal Fee + HST) which is the fee associated with a demolition control application; and
WHEREAS the properties remain subject to a demolition permit.
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that Council waive demolition control approval for the demolition of 72, 74 and 85 Pamilla Street and allow the applicant to proceed directly to demolition permits; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that 72 and 74 Pamilla Street be sodded, mulch-covered or soft landscaped following demolition and prior to transfer to the City, and 85 Pamilla Street be sodded and fenced, respectfully, in accordance with the Property Standards By-law; and
BE IT FURTHER REVOLVED that the waiver from Demolition Control be void if the corresponding demolition permits are not issued within two years of Council decision.

motions.motion_text:
That the Rules of Procedure be suspended to consider the following motion as the anniversary will take place before the next regular meeting of Council.
WHEREAS Porter Airlines began its first commercial service between Toronto Billy Bishop Island Airport and Ottawa International Airport on October 23, 2006,
WHEREAS over the last 20 years, Porter Airlines has expanded its service across North America, including 32 direct flights from Ottawa,
WHEREAS additional direct flights provide better service to passengers and makes flying to/from Ottawa a more seamless experience,
WHEREAS Porter’s investment in a maintenance hanger and crew base at the Ottawa International Airport further solidifies Porter’s long term commitment in Ottawa, providing additional economic benefits and jobs,
WHEREAS Ottawa is hub airport within Porter’s network and is a growing connection city for Porter passengers,
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that Ottawa City Council celebrate this milestone and congratulates Porter Airlines on its 20th anniversary, while extending our appreciation for the investment they have made in Ottawa and encourage Porter to pursue more direct flights from/to Ottawa.

sub_agendas_items.title: Feasibility Review of Future Park Space

motions.motion_text:
WHEREAS there is a desire from residents to create more park space and community gathering space in the central part of the Fernbank community, due to increasing development pressures; and
WHEREAS there is an existing open space owned by the City of Ottawa along the Trans Canada Trail immediately east of Robert Grant Avenue of approximately 3,800 square metres; and
WHEREAS this unaddressed parcel of land is not suitable for housing or other development; and
WHEREAS Village Square Park in Stittsville is located on a similar-sized piece of land along the Trans Canada Trail at Abbott Street; and
WHEREAS there is a surplus of funding in the Ward 6 Stittsville Cash In Lieu of Parkland account.
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that staff be directed to review the feasibility of adapting this parcel of land as a future park space, identifying any constraints, required studies, and any other considerations and report back to Council in Q1 2027 with their findings.

sub_agendas_items.title: OCC-2026-23 - Capacity Pressures at the Leitrim Station Park and Ride
sub_agendas_items.minutes:
Submitted by Councillor S. Desroches
Since the beginning of September, the Leitrim Station Park and Ride has experienced sustained capacity pressures, with the City’s Mobility Dashboard showing average utilization above 98 per cent for multiple weeks. Residents have reported arriving after 8:00 a.m. and being unable to find a parking space, potentially resulting in commuters driving to their destination rather than taking Line 2.
In July, the City announced the Transportation and Mobility Strategy and Action Plan in response to increased travel demand. As part of this work, staff identified an urgent need to expand the Bowesville Station Park and Ride and are advancing plans on an accelerated timeline to more than double its capacity, from approximately 800 to 1,800 spaces.
The accelerated Bowesville expansion demonstrates the City’s ability to adapt its plans to actual travel patterns and demonstrated demand. Given the documented capacity pressures now being experienced at Leitrim Station, I would like City staff to answer the following questions:
